tree: Manual dialing makes follow-up slow and uneven.

tree.style: margin: 18px 0 0; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.65; color: #40514a; text-wrap: pretty;

tree: Copying numbers from a spreadsheet, dialing by hand and writing notes afterward means fewer calls and patchy records. Some customers get called twice; others never hear back.

tree.style: margin: 18px 0 0; font-size: 18px; line-height: 1.65; color: #40514a; text-wrap: pretty;

tree: How are consent and do-not-call rules handled?

Each contact needs a consent source before it can be dialed. Numbers on your do-not-call list, or customers who ask not to be called, are suppressed across every list. You remain responsible for following the calling rules that apply to your business.

tree.style: border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.1); border-radius: 14px; padding: 20px 22px; background: #fff;

tree: What’s the difference between preview and power dialing?
Preview shows the record first and dials when the rep clicks. Power dials the next eligible contact automatically after the rep saves an outcome.

tree.style: border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.1); border-radius: 14px; padding: 20px 22px; background: #fff;

tree: Can I use it for cold calling purchased lists?
No. It is built for calling customers and leads who have a relationship with you and have agreed to be contacted.

tree.style: border: 1px solid rgba(16,32,26,.1); border-radius: 14px; padding: 20px 22px; background: #fff;

tree: Who should use auto dialer and power dialer?
Account-care, renewals and sales teams that follow up with existing customers and permitted leads.
